heroHeadline: Balikatan 2026 SINKEX: Japan Fires Anti-Ship Missiles Off Ilocos Norte in First PH Combat Deployment Since WWII — Marcos Arrives Cebu as 48th ASEAN Summit Opens; Atin Ito Slams China's Sandy Cay 'Planted Trash' Flag
heroSubtitle: On May 6, 2026 (Balikatan Day 17), Japan, US, Australia, and Philippine forces conducted a Ship Sinking Exercise (SINKEX) off Ilocos Norte — Japan's first combat troop deployment to the Philippines since World War II — firing anti-ship missiles to sink a decommissioned vessel in the South China Sea (Bloomberg). The same day, President Marcos arrived at Mactan-Benito Ebuen Air Base in Cebu to chair the 48th ASEAN Leaders' Summit (May 7-8), whose schedule was compressed from five to three days by presidential directive. Over 20,000 delegates from all 10 ASEAN member states are expected; the South China Sea Code of Conduct tops the agenda, though ASEAN officials — while reporting being 'encouraged by progress' — acknowledge finalization in 2026 is not expected (GMA News, RFA). The Sandy Cay 1 standoff continued to escalate: on May 5, Atin Ito declared its flag-planting mission a complete success ('China failed to stop or intimidate us'), while dismissing China's counter flag-planting as 'planted trash' and a 'copycat move' (Philstar). On May 2, CCG 3103 had shadowed the Atin Ito mission in the West Philippine Sea before the civilian coalition slipped through at night and landed at dawn on May 3. The ASEAN-EU Sustainability Summit opened May 5 in Cebu with 200+ delegates on energy transition and green finance. Balikatan 2026 — the largest-ever iteration with 17,000+ troops from 7 nations — closes with ceremonies on May 8, concurrent with the ASEAN Leaders' Summit plenary.
